Let \(P=(x,y)\). The circumcenters are
\[
O_1=\left(5,\frac{x^2+y^2-10x}{2y}\right),\quad 
O_3=\left(5,\frac{100+10x-x^2-y^2}{2(10-y)}\right),
\]
\[
O_2=\left(\frac{100+10y-x^2-y^2}{2(10-x)},5\right),\quad 
O_4=\left(\frac{x^2+y^2-10y}{2x},5\right).
\]
Thus \(O_1O_3\perp O_2O_4\). Let
\[
T=x(10-x)+y(10-y).
\]
Then
\[
O_1O_3=\frac{5T}{y(10-y)},\qquad O_2O_4=\frac{5T}{x(10-x)}.
\]
Using area \(50\):
\[
50=\frac12 O_1O_3\cdot O_2O_4
=\frac{25T^2}{2xy(10-x)(10-y)}.
\]
So
\[
\bigl(x(10-x)+y(10-y)\bigr)^2=4xy(10-x)(10-y),
\]
which gives
\[
x(10-x)=y(10-y).
\]
Hence \(x=y\) or \(x+y=10\).

Using \(PA+PB+PC+PD=23\sqrt2\), either case gives
\[
x^2+(10-x)^2=\frac{169}{2},
\]
so
\[
x=5\pm \frac{\sqrt{69}}2.
\]
Let \(t=\frac{\sqrt{69}}2\). Taking \(P=(5+t,5+t)\) gives
\[
O_1=(5,t),\quad O_2=(10+t,5),\quad O_3=(5,10+t),\quad O_4=(t,5).
\]
Then
\[
O_1O_2=O_3O_4=\sqrt{(5+t)^2+(5-t)^2}
=\sqrt{2t^2+50}
=\sqrt{\frac{169}{2}},
\]
while
\[
O_2O_3=(5+t)\sqrt2,\qquad O_4O_1=(5-t)\sqrt2.
\]
Thus the second largest length is
\[
\sqrt{\frac{169}{2}}.
\]
So \(a=169\), \(b=2\), and
\[
100a+b=16900+2=16902.
\]
\[
\boxed{16902}
\]
